title: std::array and Fixed-Size Collections
learningObjectives: Use std::array as a fixed-size standard container.
Access size and elements using its interface.
Use checked access when bounds need validation.
Traverse and modify elements using references.
Compare std::array with raw arrays and vectors.

understand.concept: std::array<T,N> is fixed-size, preserves its size, and supports container operations and checked at() access.
understand.whyItMatters: It gives fixed collections a convenient standard-library interface.
understand.explain: Use size, iteration, and at() where bounds checking is useful.

practise.guidedTask: For std::array and Fixed-Size Collections, trace each example and record the collection type, size/capacity where relevant, valid index range, values before and after each operation, and what the code prints. Identify the key boundary case.
practise.independentTask: Write a C++ mini-task focused on std::array and Fixed-Size Collections: use a small collection of values/text, perform at least three meaningful operations, and test normal, empty or boundary, and invalid-index/input cases. Explain your collection choice and expected output.
hints: Select the collection type and justify its size behavior.
